newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Downside risk pushes up Bund volatility.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Downside risk pushes up Bund volatility.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options traded on LIFFE pushed higher on Tuesday, finding strong support from expectations that the underlying futures are on the way down, traders in London said.
Concerns over the weakness of the mark unsettled the Bund market, and September futures set a low of 102.17. They were trading down 0.40 at 102.27 by 1330 GMT.

Comments from Theo Waigel that Germany was interested in a strong mark gave a temporary respite to the Bunds amid expectations of concerted currency intervention by the Group of Seven but traders said they expected it to head for support at 102.00.

"Some people think the top on the futures has formed at 103.15/14, and fear of the downside is keeping volatility up," said a trader at a French house of the LIFFE floor. "There's been a bit of struggle with the usual afternoon vol slide, but the buyers are winning."

Implied volatility opened sharply higher in the August and September options, but slowed down later. August and September vol were trading at 5.1 percent mid, after opening around the 4.9 percent level. That compares with around 4.5 percent during the previous session.

A Japanese house was a buyer of 2,000 of the 101.00 strike puts in August, and overall the volume was skewed to the put side, said a trader at a major British brokerage. In the September options, more than 5,000 of the 102.00 strike puts had traded, and strikes down to 100.00 were also active.
Traders said the market had shrugged off U.S. retail sales data, focusing instead on European issues such as whether the German repo rate is likely to rise.
"Rate hike talk is back in vogue," said one local trader. "We thought that was receding, but it's still there." -- Lisa Wilson, International Bonds Unit + 44 171 542 6137
